Roshinika is known for her profound knowledge of Jaina scriptures and philosophy, and she was a prolific writer and commentator. Her works include commentaries on the Agamashastra and the Nyayashastra, as well as original works on Jaina ethics and philosophy.

Roshinika is also mentioned in the Purana literature as the wife of the Pandava prince Bhima in the Mahabharata. In this context, she is described as a beautiful and virtuous woman who was highly respected by Bhima and his brothers. While the historical accuracy of this reference is uncertain, it underscores the reverence in which Roshinika was held in Hindu society.
